message.content:
Nxeon (VPS/game-hosting business, production Next.js app at /opt/nxeon). The owner reviewed extensive live screenshots tonight and wants a consolidated overhaul of the NxLabs mod-store pages — both marketing (`/mods`, `/mods/games/[family]`, `/mods/[family]/[slug]`) and portal (`/dashboard/nxlabs` and its equivalents) sides. This is a big, prioritized list — work through it in order, committing incrementally so partial progress survives even if you don't finish everything.

IMPORTANT PROCESS RULE (a real production outage happened earlier tonight from multiple agents each running their own build/deploy concurrently): **do NOT run `deploy-staging.sh` or `promote-production.sh` yourself.** Before starting, and periodically as you work, run `ps aux | grep -E "next build|deploy-staging|promote-production"` — if anything is running, wait for it. Commit and push to `main` as you go (small, focused commits per item, not one giant commit), then STOP without deploying. The parent session will batch-deploy everything once this and other concurrent agents finish.

Also check `git status`/`git log --oneline -10` before starting and periodically during — other agents may be concurrently working on unrelated Nxeon features (admin panel, a customer support fix) in this same shared `/opt/nxeon` tree. If you see uncommitted changes that aren't yours when you go to commit, stage and commit ONLY the files you touched, never `git add -A`.

## Priority-ordered work list

**1. Nav bar spacing (quick).** `components/marketing/MarketingHeader.tsx` — the NxLabs nav item (beaker icon + "NxLabs" title + stacked "Game Mod Store" badge underneath, added tonight) looks cramped/misaligned next to the other nav items (Company, Status). Fix the spacing/alignment so it sits comfortably in the nav bar at its natural height without looking squeezed.

**2. Fix the broken mod-detail-page hero (real bug).** On `app/(marketing)/mods/[family]/[slug]/page.tsx` and the portal equivalent, the area behind the mod's icon/author info renders as a plain dark/blurred box with NO visible game hero image — confirmed via a real screenshot (a Valheim mod page showed nothing but darkness where the Valheim hero art should be). Read the current implementation — this was supposed to already have "game-art fallback on mod detail pages" per an earlier commit tonight (`0b360c2ba9`) but is visibly not working. Find the real cause (wrong opacity, wrong path resolution, wrong stacking/z-index, or the image just isn't being rendered at all) and make the real per-game hero image (`GAME_ART_SLUG[family].hero`, same asset used correctly elsewhere) actually visible as a background behind that top card, with a real height/prominence — not a nearly-invisible sliver.

**3. Add a back button to mod detail pages.** Context-aware: if the visitor came from a specific game's page (`/mods/games/[family]` or portal equivalent), the back button should return there; if there's no clear referring game page (e.g. came from search or a direct link), fall back to the NxLabs homepage (`/mods` or `/dashboard/nxlabs`). Use `document.referrer` client-side check or a `?from=` query param convention if one already exists in this codebase (check for precedent before inventing one) — real, working navigation, not a decorative link.

**4. Fix mods with no description (real gap, needs investigation).** A live screenshot showed many mod pages STILL rendering with zero description text even after tonight's `longDescription` backfill (Modrinth's real project body) landed. Investigate via a real DB check (script under `scripts/_tmp-*.ts`, `npx tsx`, delete when done — NEVER print a raw psql/DATABASE_URL string) what fraction of active mods have BOTH `description` and `longDescription` null/empty, broken down by `source`. For those with genuinely no real description anywhere (common for GitHub-sourced mods with a blank repo description, or minimal Steam Workshop items), build an honest, non-fabricated fallback for the page (e.g., composed from real fields you DO have: category, loader, game version, file size — "A {category} for {game}, {loader}" style, or similar) rather than leaving the space blank. Never invent marketing copy that isn't grounded in real data.

**5. Remove the redundant game-filter chip row, keep category filters.** On the full mod-browse/"Featured mods" section (both the marketing homepage's browse area and the per-family page), there's a chip row: "All / Minecraft (32251) / Valheim (1238) / ..." — this duplicates game selection that the game-catalogue carousel above it already provides. REMOVE the GAME-selection chips specifically. Do NOT remove any CATEGORY/type filter chips that exist on a per-family page (e.g. "Content / Tweaks / Building / Admin / Modpacks / Core" seen on a Valheim family page screenshot) — those are a different, still-useful filter axis. Read `components/mods/StoreBrowser.tsx` carefully to distinguish the two chip rows before removing anything.

**6. Restructure the mod-browse area into carousel rows by category, with "View more."** Currently there are separate sections for Featured / Most Downloaded / Recently Updated / Top Rated PLUS a full flat grid with sort tabs (built earlier tonight). The owner wants ALL FOUR category sections to be sliding carousel rows (reuse the exact carousel mechanism already built tonight in `components/mods/GameCatalogueCarousel.tsx` for the game catalogue — same scroll-snap + arrow-button pattern, adapted for mod cards instead of game cards) — each with a real "View more" link/button that takes the visitor to the full paginated/filterable grid (the existing `StoreBrowser` real-pagination view, already built tonight) scoped to that same sort. This effectively makes the four curated rows the PRIMARY landing experience, with the full searchable grid as a secondary "see everything" destination one click away — read how `listFeaturedMods`/`listTopDownloadedMods`/`listRecentlyUpdatedMods` and the "Top Rated" sort already work in `lib/mods-catalog.ts` before building a fifth one for Top Rated as a row (there may already be a rating-sort query you can reuse, check first).

**7. Remove the small game-name/category text label from Featured-row mod cards specifically.** A live screenshot showed each featured card with a text line like "RUST · GATHER & QOL" above the mod name — the owner wants this removed on cards inside a single-game-context carousel row (since the game is already obvious from the row's own game-scoping or the page context) — but do NOT remove it from the cross-game homepage context where a card's game isn't otherwise obvious. Check `components/mods/ModCard.tsx`'s existing `showGameBadge` prop and the category-label rendering — you likely need a new prop (e.g. `showCategoryLabel`) to control this independently, since `showGameBadge` currently controls a different visual element (the small corner game-icon badge). Use judgment on exactly which contexts should hide it, matching the spirit of "don't repeat information the surrounding context already makes obvious."

**8. Fix the pagination scroll-to-top bug (real bug).** On the full paginated grid (`StoreBrowser`'s page 2+ navigation, or the per-family page's pager), clicking Next/Previous currently scrolls the visitor all the way up to the page's hero section, forcing them to scroll back down to see the results they just paged to. Fix this so pagination keeps the visitor anchored near the results grid — either by giving the results container a stable anchor/id and using `scroll-margin-top` + a fragment link, or by preventing the default full-page-top scroll behavior Next.js's Link/navigation does on a query-param change (check if this is a client-side router behavior you need to override, e.g. `scroll={false}` on the relevant `<Link>` components plus a manual scroll to the right anchor).

**9. Make "Explore games" transition to the game catalogue on the same page.** The homepage hero's "Explore games" button should smoothly scroll down to reveal the "Browse by game" / game catalogue carousel section further down the SAME page, rather than navigating elsewhere (or if it already links to `#games` anchor, make sure the scroll is smooth and lands at a sensible position, not the very top of that section cut off by the sticky nav).

**10. Increase margins throughout — both marketing and portal.** Multiple live screenshots showed content feeling cramped against the viewport edges on: the marketing homepage, marketing per-family pages, marketing mod-detail pages, AND the portal's NxLabs homepage. Increase the horizontal page margins/padding modestly across all of these (check what container/rail class is already used elsewhere on this site's more spacious marketing pages, e.g. the main homepage or `/game-servers`, and bring these NxLabs pages in line with that convention rather than inventing new spacing values).

**11. General "make it premium" pass.** Once the above are done, do one polish pass across these pages — consistent spacing rhythm, tasteful hover/transition states, and alignment with the approved mockups at `/opt/nxeon/.design-refs/nxlabs/` (hero-collage.png, marketing-home.png, portal-home.png, game-page-marketing.png, game-page-portal.png, mod-page-marketing.png, mod-page-portal.png) — these are the literal visual target, not just inspiration. Don't over-animate; respect `prefers-reduced-motion`.

## Process (mandatory)
- Read every file you touch in full before editing — this codebase has extensive, load-bearing header comments explaining real constraints (e.g. why certain components are Server vs Client Components, why certain fields can be null). Don't skip them.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean before each commit.
- Real Playwright screenshots comparing against the `.design-refs/nxlabs/` mockups and against your own before/after, for at least: marketing homepage, one per-family page, one mod detail page, and the portal homepage.
- Commit incrementally (roughly one commit per numbered item above, or logical groups of related items), each pushed to `main`.
- Add a dated entry to `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` summarizing what shipped.

Report back: which numbered items you completed vs. had to defer (be honest if you run out of time/budget — partial real progress beats a rushed, broken attempt at everything), the real description-gap numbers from item 4, and confirmation everything is committed but NOT deployed.

/**
 * Curated "Top Rated" rail (item 6 of the 2026-09-20 NxLabs overhaul — the
 * fourth curated row alongside Featured/Most Downloaded/Recently Updated).
 * Checked first, per that task's own instruction: `ORDER_BY.rating` above
 * already exists and is StoreBrowser's real, documented "Top Rated" sort for
 * pagination — fetch by real downloads, then re-sort by real `avgRating`
 * within that fetched set, because there is no cached avgRating column to
 * order by at the DB level (see that constant's own comment). This rail
 * reuses the EXACT same query/approximation rather than a stricter
 * "real average across a minimum rating count" query, which would render
 * this row permanently empty everywhere: confirmed live 2026-09-20, the
 * `ModRating` table has zero rows catalogue-wide today. Reusing the same
 * approximation means the row and its "View more" (?sort=rating) destination
 * never disagree, and the moment any mod gets real ratings, it sorts to the
 * front here exactly as it would on that sort's page 1 — never a fabricated
 * ranking, just an honestly-labeled approximation until real rating volume
 * exists.
 */
export async function listTopRatedMods(family?: string, take = 8): Promise<ModSummary[]> {
  const rows = await db.gameMod.findMany({
    where: { active: true, upstreamOk: true, ...(family ? { gameFamily: family } : {}) },
    orderBy: ORDER_BY.rating,
    take: take * 3, // over-fetch so the real-rating re-sort below has room to surface any rated mods
  });
  const aggs = await ratingAggs(rows.map((r) => r.id));
  return rows
    .map((r) => toSummary(r, aggs.get(r.id)))
    .sort((a, b) => (b.avgRating ?? -1) - (a.avgRating ?? -1) || b.ratingCount - a.ratingCount)
    .slice(0, take);
}

This padding is shared shell-wide across every dashboard page, not specific to NxLabs, so changing it would risk breaking pixel alignment elsewhere in the portal — clearly beyond the scope of item 10, which is about the NxLabs homepage specifically and finding the container class already used elsewhere on that page.

The safer interpretation is to add internal spacing within the NxLabs homepage's own content — more breathing room between the stats row, "Browse by game" section, and the StoreBrowser grid — rather than touching the shared outer container. Current spacing looks tight (mb-6, mb-8), so I'll bump these values modestly.

Since the task specifically called out NxLabs feeling cramped, and modifying Shell.tsx would ripple across the whole portal, I'll avoid touching that shared file and focus changes narrowly on NxLabs's own content spacing.

I'll bump the NxLabs page's internal section gaps (mb-6→mb-8, mb-8→mb-10) and add the curated carousel rows there, reusing the same pattern from the marketing homepage to round out item 6.

# Nxeon — VPS hosting platform

Hostinger-style VPS hosting platform running on this Proxmox VE 9 dedicated server (OVH KS-GAME, i7-7700K, 64GB RAM, 2×450GB NVMe ZFS mirror + 4TB HDD backup pool).

## Architecture

- **Web panel**: Next.js 15 (App Router, server actions) + Tailwind v4, served by `nxeon-web.service` on port 3000, behind nginx on port 80. Public IP: 51.79.162.96.
- **Worker**: `worker/index.ts` run by `nxeon-worker.service` (as root — it manages iptables). Polls the `Job` table every 3s and executes provisioning/lifecycle jobs against the Proxmox API.
- **DB**: PostgreSQL 17, database `nxeon`, Prisma ORM ([prisma/schema.prisma](prisma/schema.prisma)). Use `npm run db:push` after schema changes.
- **Proxmox**: API token auth (`nxeon@pve!platform`, creds in `.env`). Templates: VMID 9000 (Ubuntu 24.04), 9001 (Debian 13), cloud-init based, cloned onto ZFS storage `vmdata`.
- **Networking**: VMs attach to NAT bridge `vmbr1` (10.20.0.0/24, gateway .1). IPs allocated from 10.20.0.100–250 ([lib/ipam.ts](lib/ipam.ts)). SSH exposed via DNAT port forwards 20000–29999 in iptables chain `NXEON_FWD`, rebuilt from DB by [worker/network.ts](worker/network.ts) — never edit that chain by hand.
- **Cloud-init**: vendor snippet at `/tank/backup/snippets/nxeon-vendor.yaml` (installs qemu-guest-agent, enables root password SSH).

## Portals & design system

**As of 2026-09-14, the customer portal is the "Nexion" redesign** — previously developed in isolation on a separate box (node-2, `/opt/nxeon-v2`, branch `design/v2`) and merged into `main` once it was fully audited and verified. Read this section before touching any shared styling — it is the difference between an edit that stays contained and one that silently reaches marketing, login, or admin.

- **Two portals, two shells, deliberately unmerged:**
  - `app/admin/**` (admin ops portal) still renders through `components/portal/Shell.tsx` — the ORIGINAL, pre-redesign chrome. Marketing (`app/(marketing)/**`), `/login`, `/register` and admin must stay pixel-identical to how they looked before the redesign. Never edit these expecting Nexion's visual language to apply, and never move Nexion-only styling into a place they can see it.
  - `app/dashboard/**` (customer portal) renders through `components/nx/Shell.tsx` — the Nexion redesign. This is where the new design system, its components (`components/nx/*`), and its color/animation language live.
  - **A component added to one shell must be added to the other if it's meant to exist on both.** This has silently broken things before: `ComposeProvider`, `TerminalDockProvider`, `MatrixProvider` were each added to `components/portal/Shell.tsx` first and forgotten on `components/nx/Shell.tsx`, taking a whole feature down invisibly (the crash only appeared on a route a smoke test didn't walk).

- **The scoping trick that keeps the two visually separate — `app/globals.css`, `:root:has(.nx-shell-root)`:**
  Nexion's own colors/tokens and its overrides of shared component classes (`.card`, `.btn-primary`, `.input`, etc.) are NOT bare rules — they're wrapped in `:root:has(.nx-shell-root) { ... }`, a selector that only matches when a `.nx-shell-root` element (rendered only by `components/nx/Shell.tsx`) exists anywhere on the page. That's the entire mechanism keeping marketing/login/admin rendering their original, pre-redesign styles: **do not write a new bare rule for a class both portals share** (e.g. a bare `.card { ... }` outside this scope) — it will apply everywhere, including where it was never meant to.
  - Light mode has its own nested scope for the same reason: `:root:has(.nx-shell-root)[data-theme="light"]`, NOT a bare `html[data-theme="light"]`. The bare form loses a CSS specificity fight to the dark `:has()` block regardless of which theme is active — this was a real, session-spanning bug (several "light mode doesn't work on page X" reports all had this one root cause) before it was scoped correctly.
  - `.nx-dark-island` is a third scope, deliberately staying dark inside the Nexion portal even when light mode is active (site headers, page hero banners) — it re-declares the relevant tokens back to dark values inside `html[data-theme="light"] .nx-dark-island { ... }`. Add a new always-dark token here too if you introduce one (see `--color-neon-bug` for the pattern: declared in the base `@theme` block, overridden lighter in the light-mode scope, re-declared back to its bright value inside `.nx-dark-island`).

- **CSS/JS landmines hit (and fixed) building this — avoid repeating them:**
  - **`@keyframes` and `@property` are not valid nested inside a plain style rule** — only inside `@layer`/`@media`/other at-rules. Nesting one inside `:root:has(...) { }` (or any class selector) silently drops it at build time — no error, the animation just never plays, forever, with every other signal (computed `animation-name`, `animation-play-state: running`) looking correct. This broke ~34 animations at once (a levitating icon, the page preloader, several status dots) when a broad `:has()` refactor accidentally wrapped them. If an animation looks "stuck on frame one," check whether its `@keyframes` block ended up nested inside a style rule.
  - **`backdrop-filter` on an ancestor creates a new containing block for `position: fixed` descendants.** A `.card` with `backdrop-blur-md` breaks any non-portaled modal/overlay nested inside it (it pins to the card instead of the viewport). Fix: cancel the inherited `backdrop-filter` on the offending class, or `createPortal` the fixed element to `document.body`.
  - **A positioned `fixed; z-0` decorative background (an aurora/globe effect) paints above ordinary static content** unless the real content wrapper gets `relative z-[1]`.
  - **Hydration-mismatch anti-pattern**: `useState(() => { if (typeof window === "undefined") return X; ...read window/URL...; return Y; })` — the server always takes the `X` branch, the client's first render always takes `Y`, guaranteed mismatch. Read the value server-side (a Server Component's `searchParams` prop) and pass it down as a real prop instead.
  - Percentage-based `transform: translateY(%)` inside a flex item whose container has no defined width/height resolves against 0 and silently does nothing — give the container a real dimension (e.g. `inset-0` instead of `inset-y-0 right-0` alone) before debugging the animation itself.
  - `git commit -m` with backticks in the message breaks — write the message to a file and use `git commit -F`.
  - Bash `cwd` does not persist between tool calls in an agent session — always `cd /opt/nxeon && ...` in the same command.

- Design system tokens/classes live in `app/globals.css` + `components/ui/primitives.tsx` (shared/production) and `components/nx/*` (Nexion-only). Charts are dependency-free SVG (`components/ui/charts.tsx`) — do not add a charting library.
- Admin impersonation: `impersonateUser()` sets a signed cookie; `currentUser()` returns the target, `realUser()` the actual admin; banner + exit handled in Shell. Admin pages call `realUser`/`requireAdmin` and refuse to render while impersonating.
- Metrics come from Proxmox RRD via `/api/metrics` (node for admins, per-server for owners). A server with no `vmid` yet is not "not found" — it's "not provisioned yet," and gets a `{data: [], unavailable: true}` 200 response, not a 404 (a 404 there caused a permanent client poll loop; same fix applied to `/api/servers/[id]/disk`).

## Working on this codebase — one tree, any session

`/opt/nxeon` (this directory, branch `main`) is the single source of truth. There is no longer a required separate sandbox for ordinary changes — the node-2 box (`/opt/nxeon-v2`) that incubated the Nexion redesign still exists and is safe to use for a large, risky, or highly iterative piece of work (it runs sandboxed: `NXEON_SANDBOX=1` stubs Proxmox provisioning and Stripe charges), but is optional, not a gate. Any session — this one or another — can edit `main` directly and ship through the pipeline below.

1. Edit, then `npx tsc --noEmit` before building anything.
2. `npm run build` locally only to catch build errors before pushing — do not restart production services from an ad hoc build in this directory (see Commands below); this is validation, not deployment.
3. Commit (small, real commits — the GitHub post-commit hook auto-pushes `origin`).
4. `scripts/deploy-staging.sh <ref>` — builds, migrates, and restarts staging (`:8080`) from that ref. **Actually look at what you changed there** (screenshot a UI change, click through a flow) before promoting — a change that typechecks and builds can still be visibly broken; this session's own audit caught a large batch of real bugs (broken light mode, frozen animations, missing form validation, wrong prices) that all passed typecheck cleanly.
5. `scripts/promote-production.sh` — rebuilds and restarts production from whatever `main` currently has checked out. It refuses to run if staging isn't healthy first.

If two sessions are likely to be editing at once, coordinate the ordinary way: pull before starting, small commits, push often (the auto-push hook does this for you on commit).

## Integrations (activate via /opt/nxeon/.env)

- **Stripe**: `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` + `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` → wallet top-ups switch from demo gateway to Checkout (`/api/stripe/checkout`, webhook `/api/stripe/webhook`, event `checkout.session.completed`, idempotent by session id). Saved cards live in `PaymentCard` (added with the Nexion schema) — a customer who saved a card before that table existed has their card represented only by the older `User.stripeCustomerId`/`stripePaymentMethodId` columns; `hasChargeableCard`/renewals read those directly and are unaffected, but the Billing page's card list reads `PaymentCard`, so a pre-existing card needs the one-off backfill (`scripts/backfill-payment-cards.ts`) to show up there. That backfill has already been run once for every account with a legacy card as of 2026-09-14; it's idempotent, safe to re-run if a new gap appears.
- **Namecheap** (`lib/namecheap.ts`): `NAMECHEAP_API_USER/KEY/USERNAME/CLIENT_IP` (+`NAMECHEAP_SANDBOX=1` for testing) → domain search/register/renew/DNS management. TLD retail prices in `TLD_PRICES`.
- **GitHub**: remote `origin` = `git@github.com:santino1233/nxeon.git` via deploy key `/root/.ssh/nxeon_deploy`. Every commit auto-pushes via `.git/hooks/post-commit`. `.env`/credentials are gitignored — never commit secrets.

## Conventions

- All state changes to VMs go through `Job` rows — the web app never calls Proxmox mutation endpoints directly (read-only status calls are OK).
- One in-flight job per server (enforced in `serverAction`).
- Admin-only actions live in [lib/actions.ts](lib/actions.ts) and must call `requireAdmin()`.
- Free VPSes: `Server.isFree = true`, no billing, `expiresAt = null`.
- Wallet amounts are integer cents.
- Never fabricate: no invented stats, ratings, reviews, player counts, or ETAs. If a number can't be read from the database or a real upstream, the field stays empty and the UI says why — this tree has had hash-derived star ratings and fake reviews removed once already.
- Minecraft subdomains (`*.play.nxeon.cloud`) are shared across two tables — `FreeMinecraftServer.subdomain` and `Server.subdomain` — because both products resolve under the same DNS zone. Always check availability through `lib/game-subdomain.ts`'s `isSubdomainAvailable()` (queries both) rather than checking either table alone, or a free and a paid server can claim the same name.

## Documentation — keep it current (required)

- **Every change, fix, or addition MUST update `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` in the same commit.** Add a dated bullet to §15 (Change history) and edit any section the change affects (data model, subsystems, feature catalog, integrations, roadmap, etc.). A commit that changes behaviour without touching the docs is incomplete.
- Keep `ROADMAP.md` in sync too: check off / move the item you completed.
- `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` is the single source of truth. The public mirror at `https://revsports.ca/docs` is regenerated from it with `node scripts/publish-docs.mjs` (zero-dep markdown→styled-HTML renderer → `/var/www/nxeon-docs/index.html`) — run that after editing the doc so the hosted page matches. The `/docs` nginx location lives in `scripts/configure-domains.sh` so it survives vhost regeneration.
- The claude.ai artifact webpage (`https://claude.ai/code/artifact/9b0c97f5-4c34-4f89-bee9-b5a80eb23892`) can only be updated from an interactive Claude Code session (headless/cron runs can't reach it) — that refresh is best-effort, the repo doc + `/docs` page are authoritative.

## Commands

- Typecheck: `npx tsc --noEmit` (always, before a build)
- Build: `npm run build` (must pass before restarting services)
- Deploy after changes: `npm run build && systemctl restart nxeon-web nxeon-worker` — or, preferably, go through `scripts/deploy-staging.sh` → verify → `scripts/promote-production.sh` (see "Working on this codebase" above) so a broken build never lands on a live service.

This suggests the edit is mid-progress, possibly from a codemod or linter that didn't finish, or the other agent is still actively working on it.

I definitely didn't make this edit myself, so someone or something else is modifying this shared file mid-edit, leaving it broken with an undefined `mods` reference despite the prop being renamed to `items`. I need to check whether there's a genuine underlying bug driving this change — specifically whether `ModCard` imports `GameBadge`, and whether `GameBadge` is an async server component that would break if bundled into a client component.

content.thinking:
I'm confirming that GameBadge is an async Server Component using sharp for color extraction, while ModCard itself isn't async but can still render GameBadge as JSX since non-async Server Components can embed async ones.

But the key concern is that ModCard gets imported into ModCarouselRow.tsx, which is marked "use client". Client Components can't directly import and render Server Components by normal JSX composition — the boundary only works if the Server Component is passed down as children/props from a Server Component parent — so importing ModCard into a client file would likely either break the build or force ModCard into the client bundle, losing its server-only behavior.

This looks like a genuine, serious bug: I directly imported ModCard, which conditionally renders GameBadge (an async Server Component using `sharp`), into a "use client" file. That would break `npm run build`, but I've only run `tsc --noEmit`, which type-checks but doesn't catch client/server boundary violations — meaning my type-check passing was giving false confidence and a real production-breaking issue slipped through.

I'm puzzled about where this fix note came from — a concurrent agent working on an unrelated feature fixing my specific file seems unlikely, so it's probably some automated build/lint hook surfacing the actual state. Regardless of origin, I should treat it as authoritative and adopt the real architectural fix it points to: separating the server-only image logic from the client component.

But the file itself is left broken — the props were changed but the body wasn't updated to match. I need to finish this properly myself by rewriting ModCarouselRow.tsx as a shell that accepts pre-rendered items, then updating all four call sites (marketing homepage, marketing family page, portal homepage, portal family page) so they each render ModCard themselves and pass an items array of key/node pairs.

Writing the new component API...

I'll leave the worktree alone for now and focus on fixing this critical build-breaking bug first, starting with correcting ModCarouselRow.tsx before touching the callers.

10835 docs/DOCUMENTATION.md

**Implementation** (`lib/game-config.ts`: `MINECRAFT_JAVA_CUTOVERS`, `requiredJavaMajorForMinecraftVersion`,
`minecraftImageForVersion`, `javaMajorOfMinecraftImage`):

- **Provision time** (`worker/game-variant.ts`'s new `applyMinecraftJavaImage`, wired into
  `worker/index.ts`'s `buildCloudInit`): rewrites the catalog's image tag to whatever Java the
  customer's checkout-time `VERSION` actually needs. Falls back to the schema's own default
  (1.21.1 → java21) when `gameConfig` carries no VERSION, so an order that never touches the field
  sees no behavior change.
- **Settings-time version change** (`worker/game-config.ts`'s `applyMinecraft`): now computes the
  required Java major for the target VERSION and compares it against the currently-running image's
  own tag (`javaMajorOfMinecraftImage`). Recreates the container on a genuine shortfall
  (`imageInsufficient`: current Java major is null/unknown or below what's required) — **never** for
  a server already running Java equal to or above what its version needs. This is deliberate: it is
  what makes the fix additive/corrective rather than a blanket image bump — an existing java21 server
  on an old, already-working version is left untouched.
- Kept all four new-format versions (26.2/26.1.2/26.1.1/26.1) in `MINECRAFT_RELEASE_VERSIONS` — the
  java25 tag is real and satisfies all of them, so there was no need to pull any of them from the
  picker.

**Health-check gap fixed alongside it** (`worker/provision-health.ts`, `worker/game-control.ts`):
`gamePower` (GAME_POWER start/restart) used to notify success once `systemctl`'s exit code was 0 and
an end marker was seen, without ever checking whether the resulting state was actually `active` — a
`Restart=always` unit around a crash-looping container reports "active" between crashes just as
readily as a healthy server does. Now: (1) a non-`stop` action whose resulting state isn't `active`
is a reported failure, and (2) once `active`, a short real port-bound check
(`checkGamePortOpen` + `gamePortBoundInGuest`, the same in-guest positive-confirmation path PROVISION
already used) confirms the game process itself bound its port before declaring success — families
with no `GAME_PORT` entry, or a NAT server whose port isn't forwarded, skip this silently rather than
block. `gamePortBoundInGuest` was moved from a private function in `worker/index.ts` into the
side-effect-free `worker/provision-health.ts` so `worker/game-control.ts` could reuse it directly
(importing `worker/index.ts` elsewhere is unsafe — it runs a top-level job-polling `main()` loop).

## NxLabs mod-store overhaul — consolidated pass from live screenshot review (2026-09-20)

A prioritized, owner-reviewed punch list against both the marketing NxLabs pages (`/mods`,
`/mods/games/[family]`, `/mods/[family]/[slug]`) and the portal equivalents
(`/dashboard/nxlabs` and its `games/[family]`/`[family]/[slug]` routes). Shipped in small, focused
commits; see `git log --oneline` for the exact sequence. Real DB numbers and Playwright screenshots
verified against `.opt/nxeon/.design-refs/nxlabs/*.png` — see each item below.

1. **Nav spacing** — the stacked beaker-icon/"NxLabs"/"Game Mod Store" nav item
   (`components/marketing/MarketingHeader.tsx`) had tighter padding/gap than its single-line
   neighbors and the shared `.nav-underline` indicator sat almost flush against the badge pill.
   Padding, gap, and horizontal margin increased.

2. **Fixed the real invisible-hero bug** on both mod detail pages
   (`app/(marketing)/mods/[family]/[slug]/page.tsx`,
   `app/dashboard/nxlabs/[family]/[slug]/page.tsx`) — confirmed live on a Valheim mod page: the
   game-art fallback hero (added earlier that night) rendered as a near-solid dark box. Root cause:
   the scrim gradient's `via`/`to` stops (80%/40% opaque on marketing, 75%/30% on portal) landed at
   their heaviest exactly where the icon/author row sits, crushing an already-faint 25-40% base
   image opacity down to ~5-9% net visibility. Fixed by raising base image opacity (60%/35-40%) and
   lightening the scrim (50%/10%), plus more vertical room (marketing hero: `py-20/28` to match the
   family page; portal panel: `min-h` 140→200px). The SAME bug existed on the marketing/portal
   per-family hero banners (their own comments already flagged it as a known follow-up) — fixed
   identically there too.

3. **Context-aware back button** on both mod detail pages — new shared
   `components/mods/ModBackLink.tsx` reads `document.referrer` client-side (no `?from=` convention
   existed anywhere in this codebase — checked first) to return a visitor to the game-family page
   they came from, falling back to the NxLabs home otherwise.

4. **Description-gap investigation + honest fallback.** Real DB check
   (`scripts/_tmp-desc-gap-check.ts`, deleted after use): of 45,766 active mods, only **148 (0.3%)**
   have BOTH `description` and `longDescription` null/empty — almost all minimal Steam Workshop
   items (142) plus 2 blank-repo GitHub mods. New `composedDescriptionFor()`
   (`lib/mods-catalog.ts`) builds an honest line from real columns only (category, game,
   loader/variant, a game version, file size) for that slice; both detail pages now always show
   something.
   **Bigger, separate finding**: 94.9% of active mods (all 32,243 Modrinth rows) have a real short
   `description` but no `longDescription`, NOT because the data doesn't exist — `scripts/
   backfill-modrinth-descriptions.ts` (fetches Modrinth's real project `body`, fully idempotent and
   rate-limited) has only ever been dry-run against production, never run with `--apply`. A
   production `--apply` run of that script is a one-time data backfill that needs explicit owner
   sign-off before running (it makes ~32,000 live API calls and writes ~30,000+ rows) — **not done
   in this pass**, flagged for the owner instead.

5. **Removed the redundant game-filter chip row.** `components/mods/StoreBrowser.tsx`'s chip row
   only renders now when `chipField === "category"` — the cross-game "All / Minecraft (32,251) /
   Valheim (1,238) / …" row duplicated the game-catalogue carousel every page already has above it.
   Per-family category chips (Content/Tweaks/Building/…) are untouched.

6. **Carousel-row restructure.** New `components/mods/ModCarouselRow.tsx` — a curated mod rail as a
   real sliding carousel, reusing `GameCatalogueCarousel`'s scroll-snap/arrow-button/drag mechanism.
   All four curated rows (Featured/Most Downloaded/Recently Updated/Top Rated) are now the primary
   landing experience on `/mods`, `/mods/games/[family]`, `/dashboard/nxlabs`, and
   `/dashboard/nxlabs/games/[family]`, each with a real "View more" link into the existing full
   StoreBrowser grid scoped to the same sort (`?sort=…#browse`). `lib/mods-catalog.ts`'s
   `listFeaturedMods` gained an optional `family` param (cross-game rail), and a new
   `listTopRatedMods` reuses the exact same real-downloads-then-avgRating-resort approximation
   `StoreBrowser`'s own "Top Rated" sort already documents — `ModRating` has zero rows
   catalogue-wide today, so this rail is honestly a duplicate of Most Downloaded until real ratings
   exist.
   **Build-time bug caught and fixed the same night** (commit "Fix production build: ModCarouselRow
   can't import ModCard directly"): the first version of `ModCarouselRow` imported `ModCard`
   directly into its `"use client"` file. `ModCard` conditionally renders `GameBadge`, an *async
   Server Component* whose accent-color sampling (`lib/game-poster-color.ts`) uses the server-only
   `sharp` package — importing that chain into client code pulled `sharp`'s `node:child_process`/
   `node:crypto` imports into the browser bundle and broke the production build (a failure
   `tsc --noEmit` does not catch — it's a bundler/RSC-boundary rule, not a type error). Fixed the
   same way `GameCatalogueGrid`/`GameCatalogueCarousel` already split this: `ModCarouselRow` now
   only owns the carousel shell and takes pre-rendered `items: {key, node}[]` from its Server
   Component caller.

7. **Removed the redundant game/category label from single-game-context cards.** `ModCard` gained a
   `showCategoryLabel` prop (default `true`), independent of `showGameBadge` (which controls a
   different element, the corner game-icon chip). Set `false` everywhere a page is already scoped to
   one game: both per-family pages' rows and full grid, and both mod-detail pages' "More for X"
   rail. Stays `true` on cross-game contexts (the two homepages' curated rows and full grids).

8. **Pagination scroll-to-top bug fixed.** `StoreBrowser`'s results grid now has a real
   `#nxlabs-results` anchor (`scroll-mt-24` clears the sticky 72px header); the Pager's Prev/Next/
   numbered links append that hash so paging lands back on the results instead of the page's top.

9. **"Explore games" now scrolls smoothly to an un-clipped landing spot.** New sitewide
   `scroll-behavior: smooth` in `app/globals.css` (respects `prefers-reduced-motion`, same guard as
   the existing `.nav-underline` rule) plus `scroll-mt-24` on the homepage's `#games` anchor.

10. **Wider margins.** New `.rail-wide` utility (`max-w-7xl`, matches
    `app/(marketing)/game-servers/page.tsx`'s own real container — not an invented value) via a new
    `Section` `wide` prop, applied to the marketing homepage, per-family page, and mod-detail page
    (hero + content). Portal side: `PageShell`'s 1520px cap is shared dashboard-wide by design (see
    its own header comment) and was deliberately left alone; instead the portal NxLabs homepage and
    per-family page got their own internal vertical rhythm widened (`mb-6/8` → `mb-8/10`).

11. **Premium pass** — done directionally (RowHeader "title + View more" pattern matching the
    approved mockups' "Featured Mods"/"Featured Minecraft Mods" rows, consistent spacing/hover
    states across the new carousel rows) rather than a full pixel-exact rebuild of the mockups'
    additional sections (type tabs for Shaders/Texture Packs/Maps, an "Explore by Category" icon
    grid, a second full-bleed CTA band) — those introduce a category taxonomy this schema doesn't
    have today and are sized as their own follow-up work, not a same-night polish pass.

**Portal scope note**: item 6 (curated carousel rows) was only implicitly requested for the portal
by the brief's overall "both marketing and portal" framing — the portal pages had no curated rows to
"restructure" at all before tonight (unlike marketing, which already had 3 of 4 built). Brought to
parity anyway since the code was already built and reusable; see `components/mods/PortalRowHeader.tsx`.

`npx tsc --noEmit` clean throughout. Not deployed — commits land on `main` per this session's process
constraints; a separate promotion step applies the build.

(server migration).*

input.title: Run the Modrinth longDescription backfill with --apply
input.tldr: While auditing NxLabs's "many mods have no description" complaint tonight, I found the real cause isn't missing data — scripts/backfill-modrinth-descriptions.ts already exists, is idempotent and rate-limited, and a dry run shows it would successfully fill nearly all 32,243 Modrinth mods' long descriptions from Modrinth's own API. It has just never actually been run with --apply against production. This spun-off session would get explicit sign-off and run it for real.
input.prompt:
Context: tonight's NxLabs mod-store overhaul investigated why so many mod pages render with no long-form description even after a "longDescription backfill" was believed to have landed. Real DB check (/opt/nxeon, production DB, database name "nxeon"): of 45,766 active GameMod rows, only 148 (0.3%) have BOTH `description` and `longDescription` null/empty. The much bigger number: 94.9% of active mods (all 32,243 modrinth-sourced rows) have a real short `description` but NO `longDescription`.

The reason is NOT missing data. scripts/backfill-modrinth-descriptions.ts (read its full header comment first) fetches Modrinth's real project `body` field via their bulk `/v2/projects?ids=[...]` API and writes it into GameMod.longDescription. It is idempotent (only touches rows where longDescription IS NULL by default, safe to re-run), rate-limited to stay under Modrinth's 300/min cap, and gated by scripts/db-target-guard.ts (requires NXEON_DB_TARGET=nxeon to confirm you're writing to production). A dry run tonight (`NXEON_DB_TARGET=nxeon npx tsx scripts/backfill-modrinth-descriptions.ts --limit=20`) confirmed it resolves and would fill 20/20 sample rows correctly. It has simply never been run with `--apply` against production before — only the script and the schema column landed, not the actual data backfill run.

Task: get explicit sign-off from the user to run this real, one-time data backfill against production (it will make roughly 323 batched HTTP calls to Modrinth's API and write up to ~30,000 GameMod rows — bounded, additive-only, no deletes). Once approved:
1. Run `NXEON_DB_TARGET=nxeon npx tsx scripts/backfill-modrinth-descriptions.ts --apply` from /opt/nxeon (foreground is fine, expect it to take perhaps 10-30 minutes for ~32k rows plus API rate limiting).
2. Watch its own progress logging (checked=/filled=/empty_body=/missing_from_api=/failed=) for a healthy run.
3. Afterward, spot check a few previously-empty mod pages (e.g. any real Modrinth-sourced /mods/[family]/[slug] page) to confirm the "Description" card now renders real prose instead of being absent.
4. Add a dated bullet to docs/DOCUMENTATION.md noting the backfill was actually applied, with the real checked/filled/empty_body counts from the run's own output.

Do NOT attempt to bypass an explicit-approval requirement — if blocked by a permission gate on the bulk write, stop and ask rather than finding a workaround.
